difficultyReason: Single causal claim with obvious alternative explanation. Stimulus argues that switching suppliers caused cost reduction; correct answer introduces timing confound (new efficiency program launched simultaneously).
stimulus: A manufacturing firm switched to a new supplier for its component parts last year. Since making this switch, the firm's production costs have dropped by 12 percent. Therefore, switching to the new supplier was the cause of the cost reduction.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new supplier's components are more durable than those from the previous supplier.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Unrelated to the supplier switch, the firm implemented a new manufacturing efficiency program at the same time it switched suppliers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The firm's competitors have also switched to the same new supplier in recent years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The new supplier is located in a region with lower labor costs than the previous supplier's region.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The firm's profit margins have increased along with the cost reduction.

explanations.correct: By introducing an alternative cause operating at the same time as the supplier switch, this answer undermines the conclusion that the switch itself caused the cost reduction. The cost drop could instead result from the efficiency program.
explanations.A: This fact supports the value of the new supplier but does not address whether the supplier switch caused the observed cost reduction.
explanations.C: This is consistent with the supplier being a good choice but does not weaken the causal claim.
explanations.D: This actually strengthens the argument by providing a mechanism (lower labor costs) explaining why the supplier switch would reduce costs.
explanations.E: This is consistent with the cost reduction being beneficial but does not address its cause.
